key_insight: DFT-trained machine-learning surrogates efficiently model small-polaron hopping and predict charge conductivity in a battery anode material.
engineering_relevance: The workflow could accelerate conductivity assessment in energy materials, demonstrated here for Li₄Ti₅O₁₂ battery anodes rather than solar cells.
method: Use density functional theory (DFT) to calculate polaron hopping barriers.
Train ML surrogates to estimate barriers across many inequivalent configurations.
Feed surrogate predictions into a kinetic model to estimate conductivity under defected conditions.
evidence_signal: Using 154 of 3,649 symmetry-inequivalent barrier calculations, the workflow achieved over 20-fold computational efficiency and predicted room-temperature conductivity of 6.7 × 10⁻³ S/cm, within the experimental range.
watch_item: Transferability to other materials or defect conditions requires validation beyond the demonstrated Li₄Ti₅O₁₂ system.
paper_title: A Machine-learning-aided Workflow for Sampling Small Polaron Dynamics in Energy Materials
